# **1\. Executive Summary**

## **1.1 Project overview**

**VulnDesk** is a secure web application designed to streamline how security researchers, triage analysts, and system administrators report, manage, and track software vulnerabilities. Instead of relying on messy emails or shared spreadsheets, VulnDesk introduces strict data isolation, team workspaces with granular permissions, automated SLA tracking based on issue severity, and comprehensive administrative controls. The application is built using **React \+ TypeScript (Vite)** on the frontend, **FastAPI \+ SQLModel** on the backend, **Supabase PostgreSQL** for data storage, and is hosted live on **Vercel**.

## **1.2 What was built since the mid assessment**

> * **Robust JWT Authentication & Session Management:** Upgraded initial login headers to secure Argon2id password hashing with a server-side pepper. The system uses short-lived (15-minute) signed JWT access tokens alongside 7-day rotating HttpOnly refresh cookies. Users can view active sessions, revoke lost devices, update profiles, change passwords, and benefit from automatic lockout protection after 5 failed login attempts.  
> * **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Collaborative Groups:** Centralized authorization via deps.py enforces strict role boundaries (researcher, analyst, admin). Researchers enjoy strict privacy over their own submissions, while shared Group workspaces allow team collaboration with customizable create, edit, and assign rights managed exclusively by group owners.  
> * **Full Administrative Console:** Built a feature-rich admin dashboard featuring high-level KPIs, searchable user management with pagination and filters, detailed user activity inspection, session revocation, user banning with reason tracking, bulk user moderation, content cleanup tools (bulk deleting reports or groups), security event monitoring (tracking failed logins by IP and account), and CSV export capabilities.  
> * **Audit Logging & Cloud Deployment:** Added complete event tracking capturing IP addresses and User-Agent headers for security audits. Hardened production settings by locking down CORS and disabling demo fallbacks (DEMO\_MODE=false), successfully deploying the entire stack to Vercel connected to Supabase PostgreSQL.

# **Part A. Product Requirements (PRD)**

## **A1. Problem Statement**

Smaller security teams, academic research groups, and growing tech companies often handle vulnerability disclosures through casual emails, direct messages, or shared spreadsheets. These informal workflows mix unverified submissions with critical flaws, expose sensitive exploit steps to unintended eyes, lack clear assignment or response deadlines, and offer no audit history of who reviewed or changed a record.

Without structured access controls and standard lifecycle tracking, urgent security flaws slip past remediation windows, reporters remain in the dark about the status of their findings, and administrators lose visibility into suspicious logins or policy breaches.

## 

## **A2. Users and Roles**

*\[Table 2: users and roles\]*

| Role | Who They Are | Main Tasks | What They Must Never Be Able to Do |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Visitor (Guest)** | Unauthenticated user | View login/register/forgot-password pages; create a researcher account | Read, create, edit, or delete reports, groups, or admin data |
| **Researcher (researcher)** | Standard user / security reporter | Submit reports, edit/delete own New reports, manage own profile/sessions, collaborate in groups | View or modify other users' private reports; access /admin endpoints |
| **Analyst (analyst)** | Security triage reviewer | View all reports, update triage status/severity, add triage comments, view SLA dashboard | Ban users, change roles, delete other users, or access /admin/users governance |
| **Group Member / Owner** | Collaborator in a Group | Members: create, edit, or assign group reports per granted flags. Owner: rename/delete group & manage members | Non-owners cannot rename, delete, or add/remove members; members without a flag cannot perform that action |
| **Admin (admin)** | Platform administrator | Manage users (ban/unban, role change, bulk actions, revoke sessions), moderate content, view audit logs & security view, export CSVs | Change their own role, ban/delete themselves, or ban another admin |

*\[Table 3: goal and measure\]*

| ID | Goal | Measurable Success Criterion |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **G-01** | Strict multi-user data isolation | 100% of private report requests by non-owners return 403 or 404 in automated & manual tests |
| **G-02** | Short-lived, revocable sessions | Access JWT expires in \<= 15 minutes; logout or session revoke invalidates the refresh token immediately (401 on reuse) |
| **G-03** | Fine-grained team collaboration | Group members without create, edit, or assign receive 403 Forbidden; non-owners receive 403 on group delete/rename |
| **G-04** | Brute-force & banned-user protection | 5 consecutive failed logins lock the account for 15 minutes; a banned user is rejected on their very next API request |
| **G-05** | Full administrative observability | Every login, failed login, logout, password change, role change, ban, delete, and CSV export writes an AuditLog row with IP & User-Agent |

## **A4. Scope and Non-Goals**

- **In Scope:** Password security with Argon2id and pepper, JWT authentication with rotating HttpOnly cookies, active session management, user profile updates, server-side RBAC enforcement via deps.py, team groups with member permissions (create/edit/assign), automated SLA calculations (1d/2d/5d/10d), complete Admin Console features (KPI overview, user management, ban system, content moderation, audit logs, security monitoring, CSV exports), and live deployment on Vercel \+ Supabase.  
- **Out of Scope:** Third-party SMTP email integration (password reset returns a signed 15-minute token directly in response during demo mode), external OAuth/SSO login providers, and real-time synchronization with external CVE/CVSS databases.  
- **Assumptions & Constraints:** Hosted using Vercel serverless functions connected to Supabase PostgreSQL; requires standard web browsers with cookie support enabled for secure session handling.

## 

## **A5. User Stories**

*\[Table 4: user stories\]*

| ID | User Story |
| :---- | :---- |
| **US-01** | As a **Visitor**, I want to register and log in securely so that I can submit and track vulnerability reports. |
| **US-02** | As a **User**, I want to view and revoke my active sessions on my profile page so that I can sign out lost or untrusted devices. |
| **US-03** | As a **User**, I want to update my display name and change my password (verifying my current password) so that my account stays secure. |
| **US-04** | As a **Researcher**, I want my private reports hidden from other researchers so that sensitive exploit details remain confidential. |
| **US-05** | As a **Group Owner**, I want to create a shared group and assign create, edit, or assign permissions per member so teammates only have the access they need. |
| **US-06** | As a **Group Member**, I want to submit or triage reports inside my shared group according to my granted permissions so our team can collaborate. |
| **US-07** | As an **Analyst**, I want to see SLA deadlines (sla\_due\_at, is\_overdue) on the dashboard and reports list so critical bugs are triaged first. |
| **US-08** | As an **Admin**, I want to search, filter, paginate, and inspect user details (reports, groups, sessions, activity) so I can govern accounts effectively. |
| **US-09** | As an **Admin**, I want to ban/unban users with a reason (or bulk ban/unban) and revoke their sessions so abusive accounts are blocked immediately. |
| **US-10** | As an **Admin**, I want to review the Audit Log, Security View (failed logins by IP/account), and export filtered CSVs so I can investigate incidents. |

# **Part B. Software Requirements (SRS)**

## **B1. Introduction**

This SRS outlines the concrete functional behaviors, technical specifications, and security requirements of VulnDesk, providing clear guidelines for developers, evaluators, and testers.

*\[Definitions Table\]*

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **JWT (JSON Web Token)** | Compact, digitally signed (HS256) bearer token carrying sub (user ID), role, iat, and exp claims. |
| **Access Token** | Short-lived (15 min) JWT stored in frontend memory and sent in Authorization: Bearer \<token\>. |
| **Refresh Token** | Long-lived (7 days) opaque secret stored in an HttpOnly cookie and SHA-256 hashed in PostgreSQL for rotation/revocation. |
| **RBAC** | Role-Based Access Control enforcing permissions on the server based on user role, record ownership, and group membership. |
| **Audit Log** | Append-only database record (audit\_log) capturing security and moderation actions with actor, target, IP, User-Agent, and timestamp. |

**References:** RFC 7519 (JWT), OWASP ASVS v4.0 (Authentication & Access Control), FastAPI Security Documentation, Supabase PostgreSQL Documentation.

## 

## **B2. Functional Requirements**

*\[Table 5: FR-AUTH – Authentication & Session Requirements\]*

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FR-AUTH-01** | The system shall allow new users to register with a unique email, name, and validated password (\>= 8 chars). |
| **FR-AUTH-02** | The system shall hash passwords using Argon2id combined with a server-side PASSWORD\_PEPPER environment variable. |
| **FR-AUTH-03** | The system shall issue a 15-minute signed JWT access token (sub, role, iat, exp) and a 7-day HttpOnly refresh cookie on login. |
| **FR-AUTH-04** | The system shall rotate refresh tokens on /auth/refresh and invalidate the previous refresh token. |
| **FR-AUTH-05** | The system shall revoke the active refresh token and clear the HttpOnly cookie on /auth/logout. |
| **FR-AUTH-06** | The system shall allow authenticated users to list active sessions (/auth/sessions) and revoke any owned session (/auth/sessions/{id}). |
| **FR-AUTH-07** | The system shall lock an account for 15 minutes after 5 consecutive failed login attempts. |
| **FR-AUTH-08** | The system shall allow authenticated users to update their name (PATCH /auth/me) and change their password after verifying the current password. |

*\[Table 6: FR\_RBAC – Authentication, Ownership & Group Requirements\]*

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FR-RBAC-01** | The system shall enforce role scopes on the server via a single centralized RBAC module (backend/app/deps.py). |
| **FR-RBAC-02** | The system shall isolate private reports so researchers only read, edit, or delete their own New reports (returning 403 or 404 otherwise). |
| **FR-RBAC-03** | The system shall allow users to create shared groups and grant per-member can\_create, can\_edit, and can\_assign permissions. |
| **FR-RBAC-04** | The system shall restrict group renaming, deletion, and member management strictly to the group owner (403 for non-owners). |
| **FR-RBAC-05** | The system shall prevent admins from changing their own role (409), banning themselves (400), or banning another admin (403). |
| **FR-RBAC-06** | The system shall reject any request from a banned user immediately on the next request (403). |

*\[Table 7: FR-ADM – Admin Dashboard Requirements\]*

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FR-ADM-01** | The system shall provide overview counts (total\_users, banned\_users, total\_reports, total\_groups, new\_users\_7d, new\_reports\_7d). |
| **FR-ADM-02** | The system shall provide a paginated, searchable, filterable users list and a user detail view (reports, groups, sessions, activity). |
| **FR-ADM-03** | The system shall allow admins to ban/unban users with a reason, change roles, revoke all user sessions, and execute bulk ban/unban. |
| **FR-ADM-04** | The system shall allow admins to list, filter, and bulk-delete reports and delete groups under content moderation. |
| **FR-ADM-05** | The system shall provide a filterable audit log, a security view (failed logins by IP and account), and filtered CSV exports for users, reports, and audit logs. |

*\[Table 8: FR-DOMAIN – Vulnerability Intake & SLA Requirements\]*

| ID | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FR-DOMAIN-01** | The system shall validate vulnerability report submissions against the 5-rule intake policy (returning 409 Conflict on violation). |
| **FR-DOMAIN-02** | The system shall compute severity SLA deadlines (critical: 1d, high: 2d, medium: 5d, low: 10d) and expose sla\_due\_at and is\_overdue. |
| **FR-DOMAIN-03** | The system shall allow analysts and authorized group members (can\_assign) to triage report status and final severity with audit history. |

## **B3. Non-Functional Requirements**

*\[Table 9: non-functional requirements\]*

| Category | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Security** | All secrets (JWT\_SECRET\_KEY, PASSWORD\_PEPPER, DATABASE\_URL) reside in environment variables; login errors return generic messages without leaking stack traces; DEMO\_MODE=false in production. |
| **Performance** | API request latency is instrumented via X-Process-Time middleware header (target \< 500 ms per local request); list endpoints enforce pagination (page\_size \<= 100). |
| **Usability** | UI provides light/dark themes, loading/error/empty states, Esc\-cancelable confirmations, undo toasts, and keyboard shortcuts (/, Alt+D, Alt+R, Alt+N, Alt+T, ?). |
| **Reliability** | All records, sessions, groups, and audit logs persist in hosted Supabase PostgreSQL across Vercel cold starts and restarts. |
| **Maintainability** | Authorization is centralized in app/deps.py; 25 automated pytest tests verify auth, RBAC, groups, SLA, and admin safety rules. |

| Permission Flag | What It Allows Inside the Group |

*\[Table 12: admin rules\]*

| Rule | Server Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- |
| Admin cannot change own role | Returns 409 Conflict |
| Admin cannot ban or delete self | Returns 400 Bad Request / 409 Conflict |
| Admin cannot ban another admin | Returns 403 Forbidden |
| System Admin inside a private Group | Can view/moderate groups in Admin Console; cannot bypass owner-only member management as a non-owner |

| **UC-05** | Ban User with Reason | Admin | Logged in as Admin | 1\. Select user. 2\. Enter ban reason. 3\. PATCH /admin/users/{id}/ban. | Target is self (400) or another admin (403). | is\_banned=true, tokens revoked, ban logged |

## **B6. Acceptance Criteria**

*\[Table 14: acceptance criteria\]*

| ID | Given | When | Then |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **AC-01** | An expired or tampered JWT | Sent to any protected endpoint | Server returns 401 Unauthorized |
| **AC-02** | Researcher Alice and Bob's private report | Alice requests GET /reports/{bob\_id} | Server returns 404 Not Found |
| **AC-03** | Group member Bob (can\_edit=false) | Bob tries PUT /reports/{group\_report\_id} or DELETE /groups/{id} | Server returns 403 Forbidden |
| **AC-04** | A user banned by an Admin | Makes any API request with an existing token | Server rejects immediately with 403 Forbidden |
| **AC-05** | Admin A and Admin B | Admin A tries to ban Admin B | Server returns 403 Forbidden |
| **AC-06** | 5 consecutive wrong passwords | User tries a 6th login | Account is locked (423/403) and failed\_login is logged |

### 

## **C2. System Architecture**

*\[Diagram: system architecture\]*

\[Browser (React SPA)\]  
   \|-- Authorization: Bearer \<15m JWT\> (in-memory) \--\> \[Vercel FastAPI API (/api/v1)\]  
   \|-- HttpOnly Cookie: vulndesk\_refresh\_token \-------\> \[AOP Middleware \+ deps.py RBAC\]  
                                                              \|                \|  
                                                              v                v  
                                                    \[Services Layer\] \---\> \[AuditLog\]  
                                                              \|  
                                                              v  
                                                 \[Supabase PostgreSQL (:6543)\]

1. The client application keeps the short-lived access JWT in memory, attaching it as an Authorization: Bearer header with every request.  
2. Silent token refreshes automatically send the HttpOnly cookie directed specifically to /api/v1/auth endpoints (using credentials: "include").  
3. Incoming FastAPI requests pass through log\_requests\_middleware for performance monitoring and deps.py for authentication and authorization checks (get\_current\_user, require\_scopes, check\_group\_permission) before execution and persistence in Supabase PostgreSQL.

## **C4. Data Model**

Overview of core database tables stored in PostgreSQL:

- **user:** id (PK), name, email (unique), password\_hash, role (researcher\|analyst\|admin), is\_banned, ban\_reason, is\_deleted, failed\_login\_attempts, locked\_until, created\_at, updated\_at.  
- **refresh\_token:** id (PK), user\_id (FK \-\> user.id CASCADE), token\_hash (SHA-256), ip\_address, user\_agent, expires\_at, revoked\_at, created\_at.  
- **group:** id (PK), name, description, owner\_id (FK \-\> user.id CASCADE), created\_at.  
- **group\_member:** id (PK), group\_id (FK \-\> group.id CASCADE), user\_id (FK \-\> user.id CASCADE), can\_create, can\_edit, can\_assign, added\_at (UNIQUE(group\_id, user\_id)).  
- **report:** id (PK), title, description, component, steps\_to\_reproduce, proposed\_severity, final\_severity, status, reporter\_id (FK \-\> user.id), group\_id (nullable FK \-\> group.id SET NULL), created\_at, updated\_at.  
- **audit\_log:** id (PK), user\_id (nullable FK \-\> user.id SET NULL), actor\_email, action, target\_type, target\_id, details, ip\_address, user\_agent, created\_at.

*\[Diagram: ER diagram\]*

![][image2]

## **C5. API Design**

*\[endpoint list\]*

Every API endpoint is routed under /api/v1 and returns clean JSON error objects (e.g., {"detail": "..."}).

- **Auth (/api/v1/auth):** POST /register, POST /login, POST /refresh, POST /logout, GET /me, PATCH /me, GET /sessions, DELETE /sessions/{id}, POST /change-password, POST /forgot-password, POST /reset-password.  
- **Reports & Triage (/api/v1/reports):** GET /, POST /, GET /{id}, PUT /{id}, DELETE /{id}, PATCH /{id}/triage, POST /{id}/comments.  
- **Groups (/api/v1/groups):** GET /, POST /, GET /users-directory, GET /{id}, PATCH /{id}, DELETE /{id}, POST /{id}/members, DELETE /{id}/members/{uid}.  
- **Dashboard (/api/v1/dashboard):** GET /summary.  
- **Admin (/api/v1/admin, requires admin:users):** GET /overview, GET /users, GET /users/paginated, GET /users/{id}, POST /users, PATCH /users/{id}/role, PATCH /users/{id}/ban, DELETE /users/{id}/sessions, DELETE /users/{id}, POST /users/bulk-ban, POST /users/bulk-unban, GET /reports, POST /reports/bulk-delete, GET /groups, DELETE /groups/{id}, GET /audit-logs, GET /security, GET /export/users, GET /export/reports, GET /export/audit-logs.

## **C6. JWT Authentication Design**

*\[token claims\]*

> * **Claims:** sub (user ID), role, iat, exp (HS256 signed with JWT\_SECRET\_KEY).  
> * **Lifetimes:** Access token \= **15 minutes** (limits exposure if stolen); Refresh token \= **7 days** (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/v1/auth, SHA-256 hashed in DB).  
> * **Storage & XSS/CSRF Mitigation:** Access token is kept strictly in JavaScript memory (never localStorage), preventing XSS token theft; refresh token lives in an HttpOnly cookie with SameSite=Lax \+ restricted path.  
> * **Server Verification:** get\_current\_user verifies JWT signature and expiry, loads the user from DB, and rejects is\_deleted or is\_banned users (403) on every request.  
> * **Frontend 401 Handling:** On a 401 response, client.ts calls /auth/refresh once; if refresh succeeds, it retries the original request seamlessly; if refresh fails, it clears memory state and logs out. AuthContext blocks guest-content flash using an isLoading state while restoring the session on page load.

*\[Diagram: JWT sequence diagram for login, request, expiry, refresh and logout\]*

![][image3]

## **C7. RBAC Design**

*\[the reusable permission check\]*

> * Authorization executes in order: **JWT verification (get\_current\_user) \-\> Active/Not-Banned check \-\> Role Scope check (require\_scopes) \-\> Ownership or Group Permission check (check\_group\_permission) \-\> Route Handler**.

```py
def require_scopes(*required_scopes: str):
    def dependency(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
        user_scopes = ROLE_SCOPES.get(current_user.role, set())
        if not set(required_scopes).issubset(user_scopes):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Insufficient permissions")
        return current_user
    return dependency
```

> * Ownership is enforced directly in SQL queries (Report.reporter\_id \== current\_user.id or Report.group\_id.in\_(allowed\_gids)), never by fetching all rows and filtering afterward.

*\[Diagram: authorisation flow for one request\]*

![][image4]

## **C8. Admin Dashboard Design**

The admin interface in AdminUsersPage.tsx divides administrative duties across four focused tabs below the top **Overview KPI** cards:

1. **Users Management:** Real-time search, role and status filtering, pagination, safe bulk ban/unban (which skips self and other admins, returning {affected, skipped}), ban-reason logging, detailed user inspection (showing user reports, groups, sessions, and recent activity), session revocation, and CSV exports.  
2. **Content Moderation:** Comprehensive tables for reviewing and bulk-deleting reports or deleting group workspaces across the platform.  
3. **Audit Trail:** Searchable log with action filters, resolving target IDs into friendly labels (such as email addresses, group titles, or report names) with CSV export support.  
4. **Security Monitoring:** Security view aggregating failed login attempts by IP address and targeted account email, along with recent failure details.

*\[Diagram: admin pages and the endpoints they call\]*

![][image5]

*\[Table: page, endpoints, filters, actions, audit events\]*

| Admin Page / Tab | Endpoints Called | Filters & Pagination | Available Actions | Audit Events Written |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Overview & Users Tab | GET /api/v1/admin/overview GET /api/v1/admin/users/paginated POST /api/v1/admin/users PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/role PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/ban POST /api/v1/admin/users/bulk-ban POST /api/v1/admin/users/bulk-unban DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{id} GET /api/v1/admin/export/users | Search (q by name/email), role, status (active \| banned), page, page\_size | Create user, change role (non-self), ban with reason / unban (blocks self & other admins), bulk ban/unban, soft-delete, filtered CSV export | role\_change, ban, unban, delete, export |
| User Detail Modal | GET /api/v1/admin/users/{id} DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{id}/sessions | Target user\_id | Inspect user's reports, shared groups, active refresh sessions, and last 20 audit events; revoke all active sessions | session\_revoke |
| Content Moderation Tab | GET /api/v1/admin/reports POST /api/v1/admin/reports/bulk-delete GET /api/v1/admin/groups DELETE /api/v1/admin/groups/{id} GET /api/v1/admin/export/reports | Reports: search (q), severity, status, page, page\_size | Select and bulk-delete reports (cleans child comments/history), delete any group, filtered reports CSV export | delete, group\_delete, export |
| Audit Log Tab | GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs GET /api/v1/admin/export/audit-logs | action dropdown (login, failed\_login, logout, profile\_update, password\_change, session\_revoke, role\_change, ban, unban, delete, group\_create, group\_delete, export), search (q by actor/details/IP), page, page\_size | Inspect chronological events with resolved human-readable target\_label (email, group name, report title), IP, and User-Agent; filtered CSV export | export |
| Security View Tab | GET /api/v1/admin/security | Aggregated by failed\_login action | View top failed logins grouped by IP address, top failed logins grouped by account email, and last 20 failed attempts | *(Read-only monitoring)* |

## 

## **C9. Security Design and Threats**

*\[Table 17: threat, defence, file or module\]*

| Threat | Defence | Code Location |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Password DB leak | Argon2id \+ HMAC-SHA256 PASSWORD\_PEPPER | backend/app/security.py |
| Stolen access token | 15m short TTL; in-memory storage (no localStorage) | security.py, api/client.ts |
| Stolen/reused refresh token | HttpOnly cookie, SHA-256 DB hash, rotation & revocation | auth.py, auth\_service.py |
| Brute-force login | 5-attempt lockout (15m) \+ failed\_login audit logging | auth\_service.py, auth.py |
| Privilege escalation | Server-side require\_scopes \+ self/admin ban blocks | deps.py, admin.py |
| IDOR / other user's data | Query-level owner & group-member filtering | report\_service.py, deps.py |
| XSS / CSRF | React auto-escaping, in-memory JWT, SameSite=Lax cookie | client.ts, auth.py |
| CORS / Secret leaks | Explicit FRONTEND\_URL CORS; .env gitignored | main.py, .gitignore |
| SQL Injection | Parameterized SQLModel / SQLAlchemy ORM queries | services/\*.py |

## **C10. Deployment on Vercel**

Both the React SPA (dist/) and FastAPI backend serverless entry point (api/index.py) deploy directly from the main branch on Vercel, linking to Supabase PostgreSQL using its transaction pooler (port :6543). Client routing redirects non-API paths back to index.html for seamless navigation.

- **Environment Variable Names:** DATABASE\_URL, JWT\_SECRET\_KEY, PASSWORD\_PEPPER, FRONTEND\_URL, DEMO\_MODE (false), COOKIE\_SECURE (true).

*\[Diagram: deployment layout\]*

![][image6]

*\[Table: environment variable names and what each is for\]*

| Environment Variable | Where Set | What It Is For |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **DATABASE\_URL** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | PostgreSQL connection string pointing to the hosted Supabase session pooler (:6543) for persistent storage. |
| **JWT\_SECRET\_KEY** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | Secret signing key used by PyJWT (HS256) to sign and verify 15-minute access tokens and password-reset tokens. |
| **PASSWORD\_PEPPER** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | Server-side secret mixed into passwords via HMAC-SHA256 before Argon2id hashing/verification. |
| **FRONTEND\_URL** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | Deployed frontend origin (\[https\://2221656-vulndesk.vercel.app\](https\://2221656-vulndesk.vercel.app)) allowed by FastAPI's CORS middleware. |
| **DEMO\_MODE** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | Controls legacy X-Demo-User header fallback; strictly set to false in production so Bearer JWT is mandatory. |
| **COOKIE\_SECURE** | Vercel (Backend) & backend/.env | Sets the Secure flag on the HttpOnly refresh cookie (true over HTTPS in production; false on local HTTP). |
| **ACCESS\_TOKEN\_EXPIRE\_MINUTES** | backend/app/config.py / .env | Access JWT lifetime in minutes (set to 15). |
| **REFRESH\_TOKEN\_EXPIRE\_DAYS** | backend/app/config.py / .env | Refresh token cookie and DB row lifetime in days (set to 7). |
| **VITE\_API\_BASE\_URL** | Vercel (Frontend) / .env | Base API path (/api/v1) used by the React Axios/fetch client in production (zero localhost URLs). |

# **Part E. Project Management and Conclusion**

## **E1. How to Run and Test**

1. **Prerequisites:** Python 3.11+, Node.js 18+, PostgreSQL (or SQLite for local tests).  
2. **Backend Setup:**

```sh
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
# Create backend/.env from backend/.env.example
python -m app.seed
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

3. **Frontend Setup:**

```sh
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

4. **Run Tests:** cd backend && pytest \-q  
5. **Test Accounts:** Roles include admin (2 accounts), researcher (3 accounts), and analyst (1 account)

*(All commits were authored directly by NayemPathan on GitHub and deployed from main.)*

## **E3. Limitations**

- Password reset issues a signed 15-minute reset token in the API response rather than sending an external SMTP email.  
- Live Vercel serverless cold starts can add \~1–2 seconds to the first request after inactivity.

## **E4. Future Work**

1. Integrate transactional SMTP (e.g., Resend/SendGrid) for password reset emails.  
2. Add file/screenshot attachment uploads for vulnerability proof-of-concept evidence.  
3. Add webhook notifications (Slack/Discord) when a Critical SLA nears expiration.
